business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Asset management company (no physical supply chain); integration is through parentage and distribution. Operating since 1998 as a joint venture between ICICI Bank and Prudential Corporation Holdings Limited, the company leverages ICICI Bank's distribution network (7,246 branches across India as of September 30, 2025) and Eastspring's (Prudential's in-house asset manager, US$258.0 billion global assets as of December 31, 2024) multinational experience in fund management and distribution, including for the offshore advisory business. Multi-channel distribution as of September 30, 2025: 110,719 institutional and individual MFDs, 213 national distributors and 67 banks (including ICICI Bank) across 272 offices in 23 states and four union territories. Channel mix of Equity and Equity Oriented Schemes QAAUM as of September 30, 2025: MFDs 37.7%, national distributors 15.8%, direct sales 27.1%, ICICI Bank 8.3%, other banks 11.1%. Distribution is supported by a re-engineered cloud-based technology stack, the i-Invest app, distributor portal and fintech ecosystem integrations (95.3% of mutual fund purchase transactions executed digitally in the six months ended September 30, 2025). Investment management is conducted in-house with a research framework combining quantitative and qualitative analysis, an independent risk team reporting to the CEO, and a three-lines-of-control risk management structure (line management, internal controls/compliance, internal audit).

opportunities: Favorable demographics: India has the highest share of young population (15-29 years, 27%, 381.5 million individuals) among major economies, with rising urbanization and nuclear families
Increasing per capita GDP and household savings: per capita income projected to grow at a real CAGR of 5.6% from FY2025 to FY2027 (IMF), supporting savings accumulation and financial-sector deepening

Rising financial penetration and formalization: income tax return filers up from 60 million (FY2019) to 76 million (FY2024); demat accounts grew at 32.3% CAGR from FY2019 to FY2025 to 207.1 million by H1 FY2026
Digitalization tailwinds: UPI transaction volumes grew from 22.3 billion (FY2021) to 185.9 billion (FY2025), aiding financial inclusion and digital customer acquisition

Strong domestic capital markets: India's market capitalisation of Rs 449 trillion as of September 2025 and record DII participation (net Rs 3.9 trillion invested in H1 FY2026); constructive CRISIL Intelligence outlook on capital markets
Regulatory initiatives by SEBI (ASBA, block mechanism, T+1 settlement) and investor-education efforts supporting capital-market penetration
strengths: Largest AMC in India by active mutual fund QAAUM (13.3% market share as of September 30, 2025) and by equity and equity oriented schemes QAAUM (13.6% share; Rs 5,666.3 billion), per CRISIL Report

overview.business_model: Earns management fees from (i) managing mutual fund schemes as investment manager to ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, (ii) portfolio management services, (iii) managing alternative investment funds, and (iv) advisory services to offshore clients. Management fees (net of GST) were ₹27,329.5 million, 92.7% of revenue from operations of ₹29,493.8 million, for the six months ended September 30, 2025 (94.0% in FY2025); the balance comes from interest, dividend and net gain on fair value changes. Mutual Fund QAAUM was ₹10,147.6 billion and Alternates QAAUM (PMS ₹253.7 billion, AIFs ₹146.5 billion, advisory ₹329.1 billion) was ₹729.3 billion as of September 30, 2025, with higher-fee equity and equity oriented schemes at ₹5,666.3 billion. Distribution is multi-channel: 1,10,719 institutional and individual MFDs, 213 national distributors and 67 banks (including ICICI Bank), with 95.3% of mutual fund purchase transactions executed digitally in H1 FY2026.

compliance_legal.detail: All scheme expenses must fit within SEBI TER limits; SEBI's October 2025 consultation paper proposes excluding statutory levies from TER limits, reducing expense ratios, removing the extra 5 bps for exit-load schemes, sharply cutting brokerage caps and enabling voluntary performance-based expense ratios — implementation could adversely affect results.

compliance_legal.title: Changes to total expense ratio (TER) regulations could compress revenue
